TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The Sony Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset WH-1000XM4 uses BLUETOOTH® wireless technology for listening to music and making hands-free phone calls (Page 6)
- Voice guidance is provided in English for events like power on/off, Bluetooth pairing, battery status, noise canceling, and Ambient Sound Mode; users can customize language and enable/disable it via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 7)
- Initializing the headset to restore factory settings reverts the voice guidance language to default; if voice guidance is not heard after language change or software update, turn the headset off and on again (Page 8)
- Package contents include: Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset (1), USB Type-C® cable (USB-A to USB-C®, approx. 20 cm / 7.88 in.) (1), Headphone cable (approx. 1.2 m / 47.25 in.) (1), Carrying case (1), Plug adaptor for in-flight use (1) (Page 9)
- To store the headset, fold it by rotating earcups and folding one unit toward the headband, then place it in the carrying case; cables and plug adaptors should be stored in the internal holder separated by a divider (Page 10)
- The headset has a tactile dot on the left unit, headband sliders for length adjustment, noise-canceling microphones, a built-in Bluetooth antenna, and N-Mark; the left unit is marked with "L" and the right with "R" (Page 11)
- Components include: noise-canceling microphones (internal), touch sensor control panel, CUSTOM button, indicator (red/blue), power button, USB Type-C port, headphone cable input jack, voice pickup microphones, proximity sensor (Page 12)
- Indicator light patterns: turning on (flashes twice in blue, then slowly in red if ≤10% battery), turning off (lights up blue for 2 seconds), battery charge (>10% = flashes twice in blue, ≤10% = repeatedly flashes slowly in red for ~15 seconds), Bluetooth pairing mode (repeatedly flashes twice in blue), not connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~1 second), connection completed (repeatedly flashes quickly in blue for ~5 seconds), connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~5 seconds), incoming call (repeatedly flashes quickly in blue) (Page 13)
- Additional indicator patterns: headphone cable connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~5 seconds), updating software (repeatedly flashes slowly in blue), initialization completed (flashes 4 times in blue), USB Type-C port charging indicator (red) lights up while charging and turns off when complete, abnormal temperature (repeatedly flashes twice in red), abnormal charging (repeatedly flashes slowly in red) (Page 14)
- Wearing detection uses proximity and acceleration sensors to pause music and power off when removed; resumes when worn again; automatic functions can be adjusted via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 15)
- Incorrect wearing (face up/down, upside down, over caps/scarves/hair) may prevent wearing detection from working and disable touch controls; the chin must go into the housing when around the neck (Page 16)
- Wearing the headset face down or over obstructions interferes with proximity sensor and touch controls; automatic music playback pause/resume only works via Bluetooth; proximity sensor may fail if fogged or wet from sweat (Page 17)
- The headset is not waterproof; water entry may cause fire or electric shock; charging requires a USB Type-C cable and AC adaptor with at least 1.5 A output current; charging takes about 3 hours for a full battery; red charging indicator lights up during charging and turns off when complete (Page 19)

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The headset is not waterproof and may cause fire or electric shock if water enters (Page 19)
- Charging requires a supplied USB Type-C cable and a commercially available USB AC adaptor (Page 19)
- The charging indicator (red) lights up during charging and turns off automatically when complete (Page 19)
- Charging takes about 3 hours to fully charge an empty battery (Page 19)
- A USB AC adaptor must supply an output current of 1.5 A or more; otherwise, charging time increases and playback time decreases (Page 19)
- A personal computer with a standard USB port can be used for charging (Page 19)
- Charging requires the supplied USB Type-C cable; use of hubs or other cables may fail (Page 20)
- The headset turns off automatically if charging starts while it is on (Page 20)
- Charging fails if the computer enters standby or hibernation mode (Page 20)
- Battery usage hours may reduce if the headset is unused for a long time; recharge every 6 months to avoid over-discharge (Page 20)
- A red flashing charging indicator signals problems due to temperature (outside 5°C - 35°C / 41°F - 95°F) or battery issues (Page 20)
- If the charging indicator does not light up immediately, wait a moment (Page 20)
- Significant decrease in battery usage hours warrants replacement by a Sony dealer (Page 20)
- Avoid exposure to extreme temperatures, direct sunlight, moisture, sand, dust, and electrical shock (Page 20)
- Music playback time ranges from a maximum of 16 hours to 38 hours depending on settings (Page 21)
- Communication time is up to 24 hours when the noise canceling function is on (Page 21)

- About 5 hours of music playback is possible after just 10 minutes of charging (Page 21)
- The maximum operating time is 30 hours when Ambient Sound Mode is off (Page 22)
- Standby time can be up to 200 hours when both noise canceling and Ambient Sound Mode are off (Page 22)
- When a headphone cable is connected, the maximum operating time is 36 hours with both functions off (Page 22)

- The displayed charge may differ from the actual charge and should be used as a rough estimate (Page 23)
- The "Sony | Headphones Connect" app can be used to check remaining battery charge on Android smartphones and iPhone/iPod touch (Page 24)

- To turn on the headset, press and hold the power button for about 2 seconds until the blue indicator flashes (Page 25)
- The headset can be turned off using the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 26)
- The headset will automatically turn off after 15 minutes of not being worn (Page 26)
- The automatic turn-off setting can be changed via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 26)
- When storing the headset in a bag, it should be turned off as wearing detection may react incorrectly (Page 26)
- Device registration (pairing) is required for both devices before using Bluetooth (Page 27)
- Manual pairing is needed if the device does not support one-touch connection (NFC) (Page 27)

sections.summary:
SECTION: Getting started (Pages 6-19)

TOPICS: Bluetooth functionality, voice guidance, package contents, storage, headset components, indicator lights, wearing detection, charging, handling warnings

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The Sony Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset WH-1000XM4 uses BLUETOOTH® wireless technology for listening to music and making hands-free phone calls (Page 6)
- Voice guidance is provided in English for events like power on/off, Bluetooth pairing, battery status, noise canceling, and Ambient Sound Mode; users can customize language and enable/disable it via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 7)
- Initializing the headset to restore factory settings reverts the voice guidance language to default; if voice guidance is not heard after language change or software update, turn the headset off and on again (Page 8)
- Package contents include: Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset (1), USB Type-C® cable (USB-A to USB-C®, approx. 20 cm / 7.88 in.) (1), Headphone cable (approx. 1.2 m / 47.25 in.) (1), Carrying case (1), Plug adaptor for in-flight use (1) (Page 9)
- To store the headset, fold it by rotating earcups and folding one unit toward the headband, then place it in the carrying case; cables and plug adaptors should be stored in the internal holder separated by a divider (Page 10)
- The headset has a tactile dot on the left unit, headband sliders for length adjustment, noise-canceling microphones, a built-in Bluetooth antenna, and N-Mark; the left unit is marked with "L" and the right with "R" (Page 11)
- Components include: noise-canceling microphones (internal), touch sensor control panel, CUSTOM button, indicator (red/blue), power button, USB Type-C port, headphone cable input jack, voice pickup microphones, proximity sensor (Page 12)
- Indicator light patterns: turning on (flashes twice in blue, then slowly in red if ≤10% battery), turning off (lights up blue for 2 seconds), battery charge (>10% = flashes twice in blue, ≤10% = repeatedly flashes slowly in red for ~15 seconds), Bluetooth pairing mode (repeatedly flashes twice in blue), not connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~1 second), connection completed (repeatedly flashes quickly in blue for ~5 seconds), connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~5 seconds), incoming call (repeatedly flashes quickly in blue) (Page 13)
- Additional indicator patterns: headphone cable connected (repeatedly flashes in blue every ~5 seconds), updating software (repeatedly flashes slowly in blue), initialization completed (flashes 4 times in blue), USB Type-C port charging indicator (red) lights up while charging and turns off when complete, abnormal temperature (repeatedly flashes twice in red), abnormal charging (repeatedly flashes slowly in red) (Page 14)
- Wearing detection uses proximity and acceleration sensors to pause music and power off when removed; resumes when worn again; automatic functions can be adjusted via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 15)
- Incorrect wearing (face up/down, upside down, over caps/scarves/hair) may prevent wearing detection from working and disable touch controls; the chin must go into the housing when around the neck (Page 16)
- Wearing the headset face down or over obstructions interferes with proximity sensor and touch controls; automatic music playback pause/resume only works via Bluetooth; proximity sensor may fail if fogged or wet from sweat (Page 17)
- The headset is not waterproof; water entry may cause fire or electric shock; charging requires a USB Type-C cable and AC adaptor with at least 1.5 A output current; charging takes about 3 hours for a full battery; red charging indicator lights up during charging and turns off when complete (Page 19)

pages.summary:
This page from the Sony WH-1000XM4 user manual explains the indicator light system for the wireless noise-canceling headset. It details how the blue and red lights next to the power button indicate various statuses, including turning on (flashes twice in blue), turning off (lights up in blue for 2 seconds), displaying battery charge (flashes twice in blue for >10% charge, repeatedly flashes slowly in red for ≤10% charge), and Bluetooth functions like pairing mode, connection status, and incoming calls. The text specifies that low battery is indicated by a slow red flash for about 15 seconds, and that unconnected/connected status indicators turn off after a period but restart with operation.

**Text Evidence:**
- The indicator shows different statuses via blue and red lights.
- Turning on: flashes twice in blue; if battery is ≤10%, it then repeatedly flashes slowly in red for about 15 seconds.
- Turning off: lights up in blue for about 2 seconds.
- Remaining charge: More than 10% = flashes twice in blue; 10% or lower = repeatedly flashes slowly in red for about 15 seconds.
- Bluetooth pairing mode: repeatedly flashes twice in blue.
- Not connected: repeatedly flashes in blue at about 1-second intervals.
- Connection completed: repeatedly flashes quickly in blue for about 5 seconds.
- Connected: repeatedly flashes in blue at about 5-second intervals.
- Incoming call: repeatedly flashes quickly in blue.
- Unconnected and connected status indications automatically turn off after a period of time.

When you press the (power) button while the headset is on, a voice guidance indicating the remaining battery charge can be heard. "Battery about XX %" (The "XX" value indicates the approximate remaining charge.) "Battery fully charged" The remaining battery charge indicated by the voice guidance may differ from the actual remaining charge in some cases. Please use it as a rough estimate. In addition, the indicator (red) flashes for about 15 seconds if the remaining battery charge is  $10\%$  or lower when the headset is turned on. When the remaining charge becomes low A warning beep sounds and the color of the operating indicator (blue) becomes red. If you hear the voice guidance say, "Low battery, please recharge headset", charge the headset as soon as possible. When the battery becomes completely empty, a warning beep sounds, the voice guidance says, "Please recharge headset. Power off", and the headset automatically turns off. When you are using iPhone or iPod touch When the headset is connected to an iPhone or iPod touch over an HFP Bluetooth connection, it will show an icon that indicates the remaining battery charge of the headset on the screen of the iPhone or iPod touch. A: Remaining battery charge of the headset The approximate remaining charge is shown at 10 different levels. B through E are display examples. The remaining battery charge of the headset is also displayed on the widget of an iPhone or iPod touch running iOS 9 or later. For more details, refer to the operating instructions supplied with the iPhone or iPod touch. The remaining charge which is displayed may differ from the actual remaining charge in some cases. Please use it as a rough estimate. When you are using an Android™ smartphone (OS 8.1 or later) When the headset is connected to an Android smartphone via HFP Bluetooth connection, select [Settings] - [Device connection] - [Bluetooth] to display the remaining battery charge of the headset where the paired Bluetooth device is displayed on the smartphone's screen. It is displayed in 10 different levels such as “\(100\%\”, “70\%\”, “50\%\”, or “\(10\%\). For details, refer to the operating instructions of the Android smartphone. This page from the Sony WH-1000XM4 user manual details how to check the remaining battery charge of the wireless noise-canceling headset. It explains that pressing the power button while the headset is on triggers voice guidance indicating the approximate charge (e.g., "Battery about XX %") or a "Battery fully charged" message, with a note that this may differ from the actual charge. The red indicator flashes for 15 seconds if the charge is 10% or lower upon startup. A warning beep and red operating indicator signal low battery, and a final warning leads to automatic shutdown. When connected to an iPhone or iPod touch via HFP Bluetooth, the device displays a battery icon with 10 levels of charge (100%, 70%, 50%, 10% or lower). Similarly, when connected to an Android smartphone (OS 8.1 or later), the battery level is shown in 10 different levels on the Bluetooth settings screen.

elements.text: You can check the remaining battery charge of the rechargeable battery.
When you press the (power) button while the headset is on, a voice guidance indicating the remaining battery charge can be heard.
"Battery about XX %" (The "XX" value indicates the approximate remaining charge.)
The remaining battery charge indicated by the voice guidance may differ from the actual remaining charge in some cases. Please use it as a rough estimate.
In addition, the indicator (red) flashes for about 15 seconds if the remaining battery charge is  $10\%$  or lower when the headset is turned on.
When the remaining charge becomes low
A warning beep sounds and the color of the operating indicator (blue) becomes red. If you hear the voice guidance say, "Low battery, please recharge headset", charge the headset as soon as possible.
When the battery becomes completely empty, a warning beep sounds, the voice guidance says, "Please recharge headset. Power off", and the headset automatically turns off.
When you are using iPhone or iPod touch

When the headset is connected to an iPhone or iPod touch over an HFP Bluetooth connection, it will show an icon that indicates the remaining battery charge of the headset on the screen of the iPhone or iPod touch.

pages.ocr_text: One-touch connection (NFC) with an Android smartphone By touching the headset with a smartphone, the headset turns on automatically and then pairs and makes a Bluetooth connection. Compatible smartphones - NFC-compatible smartphones installed with Android 4.1 or later What is NFC? NFC (Near Field Communication) is a technology enabling short-range wireless communication between various devices, such as smartphones and IC tags. Thanks to the NFC function, data communication — for example, Bluetooth pairing — can be achieved easily by simply touching NFC-compatible devices together (i.e., at the N-Mark symbol or location designated on each device). 1 Unlock the screen of the smartphone if it is locked. 2 Turn on the smartphone's NFC function. 3 Touch the smartphone with the headset. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the pairing and connection.

pages.ocr_text: Pairing and connecting with an iPhone The operation to register the device that you wish to connect to is called "pairing". First, pair a device to use it with the headset for the first time. Before starting the operation, make sure of the following: 1 Enter pairing mode on this headset. The headset enters pairing mode automatically. In this case, proceed to step 2. When you pair a second or subsequent device (the headset has pairing information for other devices), press and hold the  $\bigcirc$  (power) button for about 7 seconds. Find the headset on the iPhone. 3. Touch the switch to turn on the Bluetooth function.

This page provides instructions and notes regarding Bluetooth pairing for a headset, specifically detailing limitations and procedures. It explains that the headset can be paired with up to 8 devices, but if a 9th device is paired, the oldest connection's information is overwritten. The page also states that pairing mode times out after 5 minutes if not completed, and outlines scenarios where re-pairing is necessary, such as when pairing information is deleted or the headset is initialized. Additionally, it clarifies that while multiple devices can be paired, music playback is limited to one device at a time. The page includes a "Hint" section directing users to further documentation and a "Related Topic" list for additional guidance.

**Text Evidence:**

- If a new device is paired after 8 devices are already paired, the registration information of the paired device with the oldest connection date is overwritten.
- Pairing mode is canceled if not established within 5 minutes.
- Re-pairing is required when pairing information is deleted, a 9th device is paired, or the headset is initialized.
- The headset can play music from only 1 paired device at a time.

The guide outlines a three-step process: pairing the headset with both devices, connecting to the music player first, and then connecting to the smartphone. A note clarifies that if the smartphone was previously connected, it may automatically re-establish a call connection upon powering on the headset, requiring disconnection before proceeding with the music player connection.

- Quick Attention Mode is useful for listening to train announcements, etc. (Page 90)

- You cannot use the Quick Attention Mode during talking on the phone (Page 91)

pages.summary:
This page from the Sony WH-1000XM4 user manual details the Ambient Sound Mode feature, which allows users to hear ambient sounds through microphones in the headset while listening to music. It explains how to activate and deactivate the mode using the CUSTOM button, with a visual diagram showing the button's location on the left earcup. The settings can be adjusted via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app, and a key feature is the Voice focus function that suppresses unwanted noise while prioritizing announcements and voices. A hint notes that settings changed in the app are stored in the headset, allowing them to be used even when connected to devices without the app.

**Text Evidence:**
- Ambient Sound Mode uses microphones in the left and right units of the headset.
- To activate, press the CUSTOM button while noise canceling is on.
- Settings can be changed by connecting the smartphone (with the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app) via Bluetooth.
- Voice focus suppresses unwanted noise while picking up announcements or people's voices.
- To turn off, press the CUSTOM button repeatedly until it cycles back to OFF.
- The function cycle is: Noise Canceling OFF / Ambient Sound Mode OFF → Noise Canceling ON → Ambient Sound Mode ON.
- Settings changed with the app are stored in the headset for use with other devices.

It explains that ambient sound may not be audible if the headset is not worn correctly or in certain environments, and warns against using the device in dangerous situations like on roads with traffic. The text also details limitations when the CUSTOM button is set to Google Assistant or Amazon Alexa, where noise canceling and ambient sound modes cannot be switched from the headset, requiring app-based control via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app. Additionally, it notes that wind noise may increase with Ambient Sound Mode enabled and suggests turning off the mode if wind noise remains significant.

**Text Evidence:**
- Ambient Sound Mode may not work correctly if the headset is not worn properly.
- Do not use the headset in places where it would be dangerous to be unable to hear ambient sounds (e.g., roads with car and bicycle traffic).
- If the CUSTOM button is set to Google Assistant or Amazon Alexa, noise canceling and Ambient Sound Mode cannot be switched from the headset.
- Settings for noise canceling and Ambient Sound Mode can be changed with the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app.
- Wind noise may increase when Ambient Sound Mode is turned on; turn off the mode if wind noise is still significant.

- Users may need to set their device beforehand to enjoy music with the desired codec (Page 96)

pages.ocr_text: Receiving a call You can enjoy a hands-free call with a smartphone or mobile phone that supports the Bluetooth profile HFP (Hands-free Profile) or HSP (Headset Profile), via Bluetooth connection. Ring tone When an incoming call arrives, a ring tone will be heard from the headset, and the indicator (blue) flashes quickly. You will hear either of following ring tones, depending on your smartphone or mobile phone. 1 Connect the headset to a smartphone or mobile phone via Bluetooth connection beforehand. When you hear the ring tone, tap the touch sensor control panel twice quickly (with an interval of about 0.4 seconds) to receive the call. When an incoming call arrives while you are listening to music, playback pauses and a ring tone will be heard from the headset. The headset has omnidirectional microphones. You can talk without worrying about the position of the microphone. If no ring tone is heard via the headset 3 Adjust the volume using the touch sensor control panel. - Increase the volume: Swipe up repeatedly until the volume reaches the desired level.

pages.summary:
This page from the Sony Help Guide provides instructions for disconnecting a Bluetooth connection after use with the Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset WH-1000XM4. It outlines a three-step process: unlocking the Bluetooth device screen if locked, disconnecting via one-touch connection (NFC) or manual operation, and turning off the headset. The guide includes voice guidance cues ("Bluetooth disconnected", "Power off") and a hint about automatic disconnection after music playback. Cross-references to related topics are provided at the bottom.

**Text Evidence:**
- Step 1: Unlock the screen of the Bluetooth device if it is locked.
- Step 2: Touch the one-touch connection (NFC) compatible device again to disconnect it; if not supported, disconnect by operating the device.
- Step 3: Turn off the headset, which triggers the "Power off" voice guidance.
- When disconnected, the voice guidance says, "Bluetooth disconnected".
- A hint states that the Bluetooth connection may terminate automatically after playing music.
- The document is for the Sony WH-1000XM4 headset and is copyrighted by Sony Corporation in 2020.

- If no voice is detected, the command will be automatically canceled (Page 112)
- The CUSTOM button can be restored to its original function via the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 112)

- The latest version of the Google app may be required (Page 114)
- The Google app may not activate from the headset depending on Android smartphone specifications (Page 114)
- The headset must be connected via Bluetooth to the Android smartphone (Page 114)
- The Google app is activated by holding the touch sensor control panel for about 2 seconds when the smartphone is in standby or playing music (Page 114)
- Voice commands are canceled after a certain time without requests (Page 114)
- The voice assist function is unavailable if the CUSTOM button is set to Amazon Alexa or if "Ok Google" is said (Page 114)

- The Google app may not be activated based on smartphone specifications or application version (Page 115)

This page from the Sony Help Guide for the Wireless Noise Canceling Stereo Headset WH-1000XM4 provides critical safety precautions and operational guidelines. It warns that the headset is not waterproof and may pose fire or electric shock hazards if water or foreign matter enters, advising immediate cessation of use and consultation with a Sony dealer. The document details specific situations to avoid, such as using the headset near sinks, in rain, or with wet hands, and outlines Bluetooth communication limitations, including a range of about 10 meters (30 feet) and potential interference in hospitals, airplanes, and areas with flammable gas. It also addresses static electricity concerns, noting that it can cause mild tingling in ears and recommending natural fiber clothing to mitigate this effect.

- Users should stop using the headset immediately and consult their nearest Sony dealer if water or foreign matter enters.
- The headset should not be used near sinks, in rain, snow, high humidity, or with wet hands.
- Bluetooth wireless technology operates within a range of about 10 m (30 feet).
- Microwave emissions from Bluetooth devices may affect electronic medical devices, especially in hospitals, near priority seating in trains, locations with inflammable gas, near automatic doors, or near fire alarms.
- On airplanes, users must follow cabin attendant instructions and use the supplied headphone cable.
- Audio playback on the headset may be delayed due to Bluetooth wireless technology characteristics.
- The headset supports security functions compliant with the Bluetooth standard, but information leaks cannot be guaranteed.
- Static electricity accumulated in the body may cause mild tingling in your ears; wearing clothes made from natural materials can reduce this effect.

sections.summary:
SECTION: Troubleshooting (Pages 128-151)

TOPICS: headset functionality issues, charging problems, pairing and connection issues, sound quality and volume problems, noise canceling effectiveness, touch sensor control panel operation, battery life and operating time, Bluetooth interference, device registration and factory settings

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- If the headset does not function as expected, users should try charging, resetting, or initializing it (Page 128)
- The headset cannot be turned on while charging; ensure the battery is fully charged and remove the USB Type-C cable before turning on (Page 129)
- Charging cannot be done if using a non-supplied USB Type-C cable, connections are loose, the computer is off or in sleep mode, or Windows 8.1 needs updating; solutions include checking connections, waking the computer, updating Windows, restarting the computer, and resetting the headset (Page 130)
- Charging time is too long if connected via a USB hub, using a USB AC adapter with less than 1.5 A output current, or using a non-supplied USB Type-C cable; solutions include direct connection, using a 1.5 A+ adapter, and using the supplied cable (Page 131)
- Available operating time is short due to features like Equalizer or DSEE Extreme; battery performance may improve after a few recharges; charge every 6 months if stored long-term; optimal charging temperature is 15°C to 35°C (59°F - 95°F); replace the battery if usage hours decrease significantly (Page 132)
- The headset cannot be charged when connected to a computer if the USB Type-C cable is not properly connected, the connection is through a USB hub, or there is a problem with the USB port; solutions include checking the cable, ensuring a direct connection, and trying another USB port (Page 133)
- The remaining battery charge is not displayed on smartphone screens unless the device is an iOS device supporting HFP or an Android smartphone running OS 8.1 or later connected via HFP (Page 134)
- No sound can occur if devices are off, Bluetooth connections are incorrect (A2DP, HFP, HSP), multipoint connection sends silent signals, or Speak-to-Chat is disabled; solutions include checking power, Bluetooth settings, stopping playback on the first device, shutting down its application, checking the headphone cable, turning up volume, ensuring playback, and resetting the headset (Page 135)
- Low sound level can be resolved by turning up the volume on both the headset and connected device and re-establishing the Bluetooth connection (Page 136)
- Low sound quality during video calls may be due to communication line conditions; use A2DP for computer connections; LDAC cannot be used for music playback when "Connect to 2 devices simultaneously" is enabled in the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app (Page 137)
- Sound skips may occur due to Bluetooth interference from human bodies, metal objects, wireless LAN devices (2.4 GHz), or other wireless audio equipment; solutions include setting the headset to "Priority on stable connection" mode, removing obstacles between antennas, increasing distance from wireless LAN devices (at least 10 m / 30 feet), turning off wireless LAN devices, restarting playback devices, and reconnecting (Page 138)
- Insufficient noise canceling can be addressed by ensuring the noise canceling function is on, adjusting headset position, checking Adaptive Sound Control and CUSTOM button settings in the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app, and setting Ambient Sound Control to noise canceling mode; noise canceling is effective for low-frequency sounds (airplanes, trains) but less so for high-frequency sounds (human voices) (Page 139)
- Pairing cannot be done if the headset and device are more than 1 meter apart; enter pairing mode by holding the power button for 7 seconds or more; delete pairing information from the device if pairing fails after initialization or repair (Page 140)
- One-touch connection (NFC) does not work if the smartphone is not close to the N-mark, NFC/Bluetooth are off, the phone case is on, the headset is charging, or a headphone cable is connected; solutions include keeping the phone close, enabling NFC/Bluetooth, removing the case, avoiding charging, and disconnecting the cable (Page 141)
- Unable to make a Bluetooth connection can be resolved by verifying power and Bluetooth settings, managing automatic connections, checking sleep mode, and re-pairing devices; restarting playback devices may help (Page 142)
- Distorted sound can be prevented by keeping the headset away from microwave ovens and wireless LAN devices (Page 143)
- The headset does not operate properly if worn incorrectly (face up/down, upside down, over a cap/scarf); reset the headset (does not delete pairing info) or initialize it to restore factory settings (Page 144)
- Cannot hear a person on a call can be fixed by checking power/volume, verifying audio settings, re-establishing Bluetooth connection, and answering calls by stopping playback and tapping the touch sensor control panel twice quickly (with an interval of about 0.4 seconds) (Page 145)
- Low voice from callers can be resolved by turning up the volume of both the headset and the connected device (Page 146)
- The touch sensor control panel on the right unit requires specific swipe motions: forward/backward swipes must be perpendicular to the headband, up/down swipes must be parallel to the headband; it will not operate correctly with fingernails, gloves, or when not worn; music playback pauses automatically during Speak-to-Chat (Page 147)
- When connected to a computer, touch sensor control panel operation may be disabled depending on the application; Quick Attention Mode cannot be used during phone calls (Page 148)
- Music playback may not stop when the headset is removed due to computer application behavior, not a malfunction; users should control playback through the computer application; if ambient sound is heard unintentionally, check [Ambient Sound Control] settings in the "Sony | Headphones Connect" app and set it to [Noise Canceling Mode] (Page 149)
- Resetting the headset involves pressing both the power button and CUSTOM button simultaneously while charging; this does not delete device registration information (Page 150)
- Initializing the headset to restore factory settings involves turning it off, disconnecting the USB Type-C cable, and pressing and holding both the power and CUSTOM buttons for 7 seconds or more until the blue indicator flashes four times; this resets volume settings and deletes all pairing information, requiring re-pairing; software updates are retained, but changing the voice guidance language reverts it to factory settings (Page 151)

pages.ocr_text: Initializing the headset to restore factory settings If the headset does not operate correctly even after resetting, initialize the headset. Turn off the headset while the USB Type-C cable is disconnected and then press and hold the (power) button and the CUSTOM button simultaneously for 7 seconds or more. The indicator (blue) flashes 4 times (  $\bullet$ $\bullet$ $\bullet$  ), and the headset is initialized. This operation resets volume settings, etc. to the factory settings, and deletes all pairing information. pages.summary:
This page from the Sony Help Guide provides instructions for initializing the WH-1000XM4 wireless noise-canceling stereo headset to restore factory settings. It details the procedure of turning off the headset, disconnecting the USB Type-C cable, and pressing and holding both the power and CUSTOM buttons for 7 seconds or more until the blue indicator flashes four times. The initialization resets volume settings and deletes all pairing information, requiring re-pairing with devices. A note section clarifies that software updates are retained after initialization and that changing the voice guidance language will revert it to factory settings upon initialization. The document is copyrighted by Sony Corporation in 2020.

**Text Evidence:**
- The headset model is WH-1000XM4.
- Initialization is required if the headset does not operate correctly even after resetting.
- The process involves holding the power button and CUSTOM button simultaneously for 7 seconds or more while the USB Type-C cable is disconnected.
- The blue indicator flashes 4 times (● ● ● ●) to confirm initialization.
- This operation resets volume settings and deletes all pairing information.
- After initialization, pairing information must be deleted from the device and re-paired.
- If issues persist after initialization, users should consult their nearest Sony dealer.
- Software updates are retained even after initialization.
- Changing the voice guidance language will return it to factory setting upon initialization.
